correctness.rationale: For prime powers, \(p^m=mp^2\) reduces to \(m=p^{m-2}\), giving only \(3^3\) and \(2^4\). For two odd primes, parity forces one exponent even and one odd. The exponent-one odd branch has a square discriminant whose factorization forces \(p^{2A-1}\le4A\), leaving only a direct impossible case. When the odd exponent is at least three, reduction modulo each prime square forces \(q^2\mid A\) and \(p^2\mid2B+1\), after which the divided equation has an exponentially large left side and linear right side. In the \(2^kp^{2B}\) branch, \(p^2\mid k\) and the same growth contradiction applies. All quantifiers and boundary cases are covered. The packaged verifier independently checks a broad finite grid.

value.rationale: The source devoted an entire section to eliminating forms for \(T^*(2)\), and later discoveries show the global fixed-point problem is nontrivial. The support-at-most-two classification is a natural structural boundary: it proves every nontrivial fixed point must enter the genuinely multi-prime regime. This is an infinite, exact classification rather than a bounded search or an arbitrary slice, and it sharpens the source’s necessary conditions into a complete theorem.
